versions.summary: The first public release. Nearly all of it came out of using the plugin in a real client, which is where the things a design cannot predict turn up.
added: A switcher on the front of the bar. One press swaps between your favourites, everything, a single role, a category, or one of your own tags.

Sorting the game's own gearset list, when you ask it to. It never happens on its own, it keeps the order it found so you can put it back, and it stops at the first move that does not land where it was aimed.
The game's own role symbols, so the bar looks like the rest of the interface rather than like a guest.
The role's colour under the pointer: blue for tanks, green for healers, red for damage.
Pick several gearsets at once with control or shift and edit them together, or select all of them.
changed: The bar follows the order set in the library. Two settings for one question could disagree, and one of them had to go.
A favourite is what is on the bar. They used to be two marks with a rule between them that nobody could explain.
Icons start at 30 pixels rather than 40, which sits better beside the game's own hotbars.
The bar keeps itself inside the screen. It wraps to more rows or more columns rather than running off an edge, and it never leaves a gearset out.
fixed: The role order in the settings grew every time the plugin loaded.
A set with a missing piece can be equipped again. The game offers you a substitute, which is not Gearbook's decision to take away.
A locked bar can be unlocked from any icon.
Tooltips no longer flicker before they settle.
removed: The entry next to the clock. Gearbook's bar is on screen all the time and every icon on it opens a menu, so the entry bought nothing.

versions.summary: The first version. A bar you can click instead of filling hotbars with gearsets, and a window that lets you search and organise them.
added: A bar of job icons. One click switches. Put it where you like, then lock it so it stays there.
A library window with a search that covers names, jobs, tags and your own notes.
Favourites, your own tags, and a note per gearset.
Filters by role and category, plus incomplete sets, sets on the bar, and sets linked to a glamour plate.
Saved views, so a filter you use every week is one click rather than five.
Three levels of filter panel, from favourites only to everything, so the window can be as simple as you want it.
Warnings where two of your gearsets share a job and a name, which the game itself cannot help you with.
Text commands for everything, so it all works from a macro.
German and English, following whatever language Dalamud is set to unless you pick one.
